reason: S1 introduces a material global-state lifecycle in which YulStringRepository::reset clears interned strings and invokes callbacks that invalidate cached EVM and Wasm dialects. H0 directly constructs AssemblyStack and never calls StandardCompiler::compile, solidity_free, or YulStringRepository::reset, so it cannot exercise the new reset-and-rebuild transition or repeated compilation across that transition. This gap did not exist in S0 because the reset API, reset callbacks, and cache invalidation protocol were introduced by this commit.
evidence: YulStringRepository::reset is new and executes every function in resetCallbacks() before replacing instance() with a fresh YulStringRepository.
StandardCompiler::compile now calls YulStringRepository::reset at its entry, and solidity_free now calls yul::YulStringRepository::reset.
EVMDialect::looseAssemblyForEVM, strictAssemblyForEVM, strictAssemblyForEVMObjects, and yulForEVM now register ResetCallback objects that clear their static dialects maps.
WasmDialect::instance now stores its singleton in a unique_ptr and registers a ResetCallback that resets it.
Every H0 target uses AssemblyStack directly; none invokes StandardCompiler::compile, solidity_free, or YulStringRepository::reset.

The differential harnesses call EVMDialect::strictAssemblyForEVMObjects, but without a subsequent reset they exercise cache construction only, not the newly added invalidation and reconstruction protocol.
recommended_action: Add a harness path that performs repeated parse/optimize/assemble or interpret operations with an explicit YulStringRepository::reset between complete operations, ensuring all AssemblyStack and dialect references are destroyed before reset; alternatively fuzz repeated calls through StandardCompiler::compile, whose S1 entry protocol performs the reset automatically.
